title: Session of Eastland Presbyterian Church, Memphis, Tennessee v. Covenant Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint found invalid/not sustained. The Judicial Commission held that Tim McKeown was not employed in a ministerial capacity, so the challenged presbytery action did not establish the alleged constitutional violation. Its report expressly stated that the decision did not imply that employing McKeown in a ministerial capacity would have violated the Constitution. The Assembly adopted the report as its action and judgment.
first_summary: A session complained that Covenant Presbytery violated PCA standards by approving a divorced and remarried man's summer employment in a ministerial capacity. The Judicial Commission found the complaint invalid because McKeown was not employed in a ministerial capacity. The Assembly adopted the report as its action and judgment.
summary: A session complained that Covenant Presbytery violated PCA standards by approving the summer employment of a divorced and remarried man in a ministerial capacity. The Judicial Commission found the complaint invalid, holding that McKeown was not employed in a ministerial capacity. It expressly did not decide whether such employment would violate the Constitution. The General Assembly adopted the report as its action and judgment, leaving the presbytery's action undisturbed.

sources.supports: Identity, complaint, Commission report, reasoning, and Assembly adoption.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Source lines 1-3 identify 4-13, Committee on Judicial Business, 4th Assembly (1976), and disposition. Lines 34-38 contain the Judicial Commission report; line 50 states the Assembly adopted the report as its action and judgment.
evidence_notes.dispute: Lines 13-17 and 30 show Eastland Session complained that Covenant Presbytery, by its July 6, 1976 action and April approval, allowed Tim McKeown's summer employment in a ministerial capacity despite his divorce and remarriage, allegedly violating 2 Timothy 3 and WCF 24.5. Line 38 frames the challenged action as employing McKeown as a summer worker.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Lines 34-38: the Commission found the complaint invalid because McKeown was not employed in a ministerial capacity; the parenthetical expressly declined to imply that ministerial employment would violate the Constitution. Line 50: Assembly adopted the report.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The adopted decision is limited to McKeown's non-ministerial capacity. It does not resolve whether a divorced and remarried man may be employed in a ministerial capacity, and the complaint's constitutional allegations are not adopted findings. The source also does not reproduce the presbytery's attached answer or the tape transcript.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No separate incorporated decision is supplied. The operative adopted decision is the Judicial Commission report at lines 34-38, adopted at line 50.

source_limits: Short extracted record; the adopted report is a single paragraph. The Presbytery's attached answer, tape transcript, and any lower-court proceedings referenced by the complaint are not reproduced, so the synopsis relies on the Commission's stated ground and the Assembly's adoption.
